Primary Source: Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin, and Rock — GPTs are GPTs; O*NET-SOC task rubric
Interpretation Boundary: Theoretical share of tasks exposed to LLM capabilities or LLM-powered software. Not observed use, automation, displacement, job loss, productivity, or a forecast; retained occupation summaries are unweighted.

Evidence Layer: Workforce labor demand mobility and separation
Primary Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
Frequency / Coverage: Monthly; January 2020–June 2026; four broad labor markets
Interpretation Boundary: Job openings, hires, quits, and layoffs-and-discharges rates provide broad labor-market context. They do not isolate AI-specific vacancies or worker transitions.

Primary Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Labor Productivity and Costs
Interpretation Boundary: Economy-wide labor productivity, real hourly compensation, and labor-share indexes. Their movement is not attributed to AI alone.

Evidence Layer: Real median earnings and broad participation
Primary Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Current Population Survey
Frequency / Coverage: Quarterly; 2020 Q1–2026 Q2; seven retained worker groups
Interpretation Boundary: Real median weekly earnings for full-time wage and salary workers. Excludes wealth, benefits, household composition, part-time and self-employed workers; demographic comparisons do not control for occupation, hours, education, age, or geography.
